Three-time major champion Padraig Harrington has been named as one of Luke Donald's vice-captains for the Ryder Cup at Adare Manor, in the Republic of Ireland, in 2027. The 54-year-old Dubliner joins the Molinari brothers Edoardo and Francesco in Team Europe's backroom team as they bid for a third consecutive victory over USA.

Harrington played in six Ryder Cups for Team Europe and was a vice-captain on three occasions before captaining the side for the unsuccessful 2021 Ryder Cup at Whistling Straits.

Golf.title: Tiger and Phil vanished from this major season. But at Lytham, history lingers
Golf.summary: Tiger and Phil’s absence looms over the end of major season. So too does Annika’s Grand Slam victory at Lytham, host of this Women’s Open. The post Tiger and Phil vanished from this major season. But at Lytham, history lingers appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Women’s Open Championship is being held this week at Royal Lytham, where Annika Sorenstam completed her career grand slam in 2003. A few months earlier, she had played in a PGA Tour event, at Colonial. Interest in Annika, 23 summers ago, was high, intensely so, and her golf, like her personality and her language, was memorably precise.

I was once following her in a tournament round during this time period and heard Annika ask a playing partner to mark her ball on the green before Annika played a shot—from 130 or more yards out. After the round, I told Annika that I had never heard a player make such a request, not from that distance. “You should watch me play more golf,” Annika said in her no-nonsense way. Ah-nee-KAH. I often wondered how she would adapt to life in Florida—she was so Swedish. Nelly Korda, a child of European parents herself and the reigning U.S. Open winner, has a great opportunity this week to make her own linksland mark on the game, by winning her first Open Championship in the very place where Annika won hers.

Golf.title: 5 keys to help you unlock more speed and master the high bomb
Golf.summary: Want more distance off the tee? Learn to hit a high, towering drive with these five simple keys from a Top 100 Teacher. The post 5 keys to help you unlock more speed and master the high bomb appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Every golfer knows the feeling. You step onto a tee box with a wide-open fairway and only one thing on your mind: “Time to let the big dog eat.” Unfortunately, that’s usually when things go sideways.

Instead of creating more speed, most golfers try to manufacture it — swinging harder, tensing up and throwing their sequence out of sync. Ironically, the harder they chase distance, the less of it they find.

Golf.title: The new Arccos app takes a big step forward to help golfers improve
Golf.summary: Arccos Golf has always been great at giving players the "what" and the "why," but the new app update offers something more. The post The new Arccos app takes a big step forward to help golfers improve appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I’ve now been using Arccos for about four months, and it truly has changed the way that I look at my game. About a month ago, they launched an update to their app, and everything I thought I learned suddenly had a different perspective. Arccos has always explored the “what” in your game; some may even say it’s covered the “why.” But now it’s exploring the “how”.

Let’s dive into the new Arccos app update. The app has expanded. There’s now more information available, more swipes to be had, and more reason than ever to spend time in the app after your round. The new software update has also improved the accuracy of all of their algorithms, including the features integrated with Arccos Air and the Arccos Smart Laser.

Golf.title: Don't make this common mistake when practicing your golf swing
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Kevin Sprecher explains the right — and wrong — ways to practice your golf swing on the range. The post Don’t make this common mistake when practicing your golf swing appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When golfers practice, most become overly focused on hitting the ball. They may start with the intention of working on a swing change, but as soon as the ball is placed in front of them, their attention shifts to making contact and producing a “good” shot.

The result is usually the same familiar swing. When you are working on your mechanics, the goal should not be to hit the ball. Instead, the goal is to make the new swing and observe how that motion affects the ball. The ball provides feedback, but it should not control the movement.

Golf.title: LIV Golf set to cancel Michigan tournament

Golf.body:
LIV Golf is planning to announce on Wednesday that it won’t hold its season-ending event in Michigan, the league’s Team Championship, according to sources who were briefed on the league’s plans.

The move comes just a week after LIV player Martin Kaymer told multiple outlets it was “highly unlikely” the tournament would take place amid the league’s search for new investment. The Detroit News also reported last week that there had been no infrastructure buildout at The Cardinal at Saint John’s Resort for the tournament, which was set for Aug. 27-30. It wasn’t clear if LIV would try and make one of its remaining two tournaments into a team championship-style event.

Golf.title: PGA Tour's latest schedule shakeup features a new sponsor (and surprise venue)
Golf.summary: The PGA Tour announced a major shakeup to its future schedule on Tuesday, with a specific focus on its annual event in Napa. The post PGA Tour’s latest schedule shakeup features a new sponsor (and surprise venue) appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When the PGA Tour descended upon the Travelers Championship in June to announce major changes to the future of professional golf, at least some in the golf world rolled their eyes.

The changes as outlined by the Tour had been in the works for months … and expected by many inside the sport’s orbit for roughly as long. The real excitement wasn’t going to be laid out in a carefully choreographed press conference, it was going to be scrapped, clawed and cudgeled over in the back rooms and board meetings where golf’s business really gets done. In other words, it was going to be up to the sponsors.

Golf.title: 10 big PGA Tour names sit on 2 different bubbles of the playoffs
Golf.summary: With just two weeks remaining in the regular season, several of the PGA Tour's big names find themselves on a FedEx Cup Playoffs bubble. The post 10 big PGA Tour names sit on 2 different bubbles of the playoffs appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Jackson Koivun’s “Hello, world!” win at the 3M Open vaulted him onto the FedEx Cup Playoffs bubble with two weeks to play. Koivun, who held off World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler in Minnesota, now sits at No. 70 in the standings with two weeks to play before the first playoff event in Memphis.

While Koivun, who will be back in action at this week’s Rocket Classic, is currently on the right side of the bubble, several other popular names find themselves on the outside looking in with the clock ticking. Others find themselves inside the top 70 but with work to do to get to the BMW Championship and ensure their spot in the Signature Events in 2027. With the PGA Tour heading to a two-tier system in 2028 and the eligibility criteria for the 2028 Championship Series (Track 1) being determined before the 2027 season, having access to the biggest events is vital to getting a leg up in the race to secure a spot in the Championship Series in 2028.

Golf.title: 7 best portable golf launch monitors for 2026
Golf.summary: Launch monitors have always been one of golf's most fascinating and frustrating pieces of technology. They've revolutionized the way we understand the golf swing, giving us instant feedback on everything from ball flight to the real causes behind slices, hooks, and inconsistent contact. But for most golfers, owning one has long felt out of reach. The post 7 best portable golf launch monitors for 2026 appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Launch monitors have always been one of golf’s most fascinating and frustrating pieces of technology. They’ve revolutionized the way we understand the golf swing, giving us instant feedback on everything from ball flight to the real causes behind slices, hooks and inconsistent contact. But for most golfers, owning one has long felt out of reach. Early launch monitors were bulky, expensive and anything but portable. Many required a dedicated computer, external power or even specially marked golf balls to function.

And perhaps the biggest obstacle? They often carried price tags that rivaled a used Honda Accord. Suffice it to say, we’ve come a long way. Today’s launch monitors are smaller, smarter, more capable and more affordable than ever before. In 2026, you can get accurate swing and ball-flight data from a device that fits in your golf bag, and you don’t have to take out a second mortgage to own one.

The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. If my ball hits the out-of-bounds marker, which blocks it from going out of bounds, does that count as going out of bounds? Thank you! – Michael Stover, age 12

Hello, Michael! It’s nice to know that Rules Guy has some young readers — and maybe someone to take over the column from him when he retires. While golf can be a harsh game at times, it’s not that harsh. The Rules of Golf aren’t opposed to good luck when it comes, and if a boundary object such as a stake prevents your ball from going OB and instead keeps it in play, then your ball is just that —in play.

Golf.title: 'Shoeless' Lucas Glover sets the record straight on 3M footwear stunt
Golf.summary: Lucas Glover didn't try to walk back what he did. He just explained why he really took his shoes off at the 3M Open. The post ‘Shoeless’ Lucas Glover sets the record straight on 3M footwear stunt appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
At this past week’s 3M Open, Lucas Glover learned what Paul McCartney discovered nearly 60 years ago when he appeared barefoot on the cover of Abbey Road: Take off your shoes in a strange place, and people are bound to talk.

And when enough people talk, they’re bound to lose track of the facts in the process. In case you missed the misguided chatter, let’s walk it back. During Sunday’s final round at TPC Twin Cities, Glover rolled in a birdie putt on the par-4 10th hole, then removed his golf shoes before reaching into the cup to retrieve his ball. The move immediately sparked speculation on Golf Channel and beyond that Glover — an outspoken critic of the AimPoint green-reading method — was making another statement about the controversial technique.

Golf.title: ‘I don’t have an ego’: LIV Golf star prepared to head to Q School if league folds
Golf.summary: ‘I don’t have an ego’: LIV Golf star prepared to head to Q School if league folds Today's Golfer
Golf.body:
Some LIV Golf players are making contingency plans for 2027, including Thomas Pieters. But the Belgian remains hopeful… When the bombshell first dropped in Mexico and LIV Golf players learned they were about to lose their financial backing, Thomas Pieters suggested he was “ready to retire”. Pieters sensed a “grim atmosphere” as rumors swirled over the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund’s imminent withdrawal and checked out as his frenzied colleagues began refreshing social media for updates.

At that stage, Pieters was certainly not agonizing over LIV’s perilous future. And three months on as the league returned from a long hiatus at JCB Golf & Country Club, it seemed very little has changed. Pieters is still relaxed as he awaits a final verdict from LIV’s chief executive Scott O’Neil, who is currently attempting to raise $350 million in new investment for the embattled league to continue operations in 2027.

Golf.title: How Callaway rebuilt its golf ball and why the Chrome Tour X settled in my bag
Golf.summary: Callaway decided to build a golf ball program that took on all challengers. With the new Chrome Tour X, they have accomplished that mission. The post How Callaway rebuilt its golf ball and why the Chrome Tour X settled in my bag appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
There is something deeply satisfying about a global golf ball factory that doesn’t try to look like a spaceship. If you roll up to Callaway’s golf ball plant in Chicopee, Massachusetts, you aren’t greeted by hyper-futuristic glass facades or floor-to-ceiling LED screens. It’s a solid, weathered brick building sitting in a quiet New England town. It looks like a place where real work gets done by people who have spent their entire lives perfecting a trade.

Truth is, they have — and like Callaway’s golf ball journey, this dedicated plant in Chicopee has seen its ups and downs. But since it started, the plant’s ethos has always been to evolve and grow the economy for the residents of this town. Needless to say, an evolution is precisely what has taken place. Inside these humble brick walls sits one of the most technologically advanced golf ball production lines in the world.

Golf.body:
BLAINE, Minn. — About an hour after he won the 3M Open on Sunday, a reporter asked Jackson Koivun an innocent question: What will you remember most from the weekend? “Just that I’ll be forever indebted to the 3M Open for helping me get my first PGA Tour win,” he said.

It was a good answer by the 21-year-old, newly turned pro, but it’s also an ironic one. It was a dream week for the 3M Open. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler entered for the first time, ticket sales skyrocketed and then Scheffler and Koivun battled down the stretch. One of the game’s brightest young stars beat out its top performer, meaning the 3M Open would always hold a special place in his heart, no matter how many more wins he piles up.

Golf.title: 'Turning point in my life': How COVID led to LPGA pro's first win in 10 years
Golf.summary: LPGA pro Jenny Shin ended a 10-year win drought Sunday at the 2026 Women's British Open, then revealed how COVID led to her victory. The post ‘Turning point in my life’: How COVID led to LPGA pro’s first win in 10 years appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
On Sunday at the 2026 ISPS HANDA Women’s Scottish Open, longtime pro Jenny Shin did something she hadn’t done in over 10 years: she won. However, just like her decade-long drought, Sunday’s win didn’t come easy. She fought off a three-bogey stretch and a charging A Lim Kim to shoot 75 and win by two shots.

“I feel like I’ve done everything wrong, just wasn’t hitting it like I was the last three days and was hitting it into bunkers, bushes, and it wasn’t fun. With the three bogeys in a row, I thought, ‘Oh, boy, I don’t know where this is going to go?'” Shin said immediately after her round. “But yeah, I hung in there and so I’m quite proud of myself. Very happy.”

Golf.body:
BLAINE, Minn. — On Sunday morning, Jackson Koivun woke up with a three-shot lead and prepared for the biggest round of his life. He sat with his father, George, like they had all week. Jackson knows what everyone is saying — the rising star with all the trophies and all the hype is out in front. He doesn’t like to pay attention to it, but sometimes it’s impossible to avoid.

“I wish people would just tone it down a little,” he told his father, while chomping on a banana and sipping a protein shake. “It’s just another day on the golf course.” His father, recounting the conversation while watching his son at TPC Twin Cities on Sunday, says Jackson’s comments were more about respect. There’s a lot of good players out on Tour, Jackson thinks. Why should he get all this attention?

Golf.body:
American rookie Jackson Koivun held his nerve to beat Scottie Scheffler by three strokes and claim his first PGA Tour win at the 3M Open on Sunday. Playing in just his third tournament since turning professional, Koivun surged into a three-shot lead on Saturday during a round of 10-under 61.

The 21-year-old then stretched his lead to five in the final round at TPC Twin Cities in Minnesota, before world number one Scheffler applied pressure. The four-time major winner began the back nine with three straight birdies, then claimed two more in the final three holes to finish with an eight-under 63 and trail compatriot Koivun by two strokes.

Golf.title: Lucas Glover's bizarre shoe removal scene at 3M Open wasn't an AimPoint protest
Golf.summary: Lucas Glover removed his shoes after making a birdie during the final round of the 3M Open. The bizarre scene sparked conversation but had it all wrong. The post Lucas Glover’s bizarre shoe removal scene at 3M Open wasn’t an AimPoint protest appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Lucas Glover appeared to have had it on Sunday at the 3M Open, but everyone had the former major champion all wrong. At least, that’s the story. The 2009 U.S. Open champion made an odd scene during the final round at TPC Twin Cities when he rolled in a birdie putt on the 10th hole and then took off his shoes to retrieve his ball out of the cup. The commentators suggested that Glover did so in protest of the AimPoint green-reading technique, something that Glover has been critical of in the past on his SiriusXM radio show.

“Statistically, [AimPoint] hasn’t helped anybody make more putts since its inception on the PGA Tour,” Glover told co-hosts Mac Barnhardt and Taylor Zarzour during an episode of his show last year. “Statistics have borne that out. It’s also kind of rude to be up near the hole, stomping around figuring out where the break is in your feet. It needs to be banned. It takes forever.”

Golf.body:
Two months ago, Nelly Korda barely curled in a three-foot putt to win the U.S. Women’s Open. It was her second consecutive major win and set off a “scrappy” LPGA plan to market the best player in the women’s game as we entered what was believed to be “The Summer of Nelly.”

After starting the season 1-2-2-T2-1-1-T8-1, there was every reason to believe that Nelly Korda’s rampant tear would continue. She was heading to Hazeltine Golf Club, a golf course that suits her strengths, for the KPMG Women’s PGA and then overseas for the Evian and AIG Women’s Open. Other than the Evian, where Korda has struggled, the schedule set up well for Korda to continue to lap the field while adding to her major total and punching her ticket to the LPGA Hall of Fame.

Golf.body:
Australia's Lucas Herbert swept to victory on the final day of the LIV UK event in Staffordshire. The 30-year-old led throughout at the JCB Golf and Country Club in Rocester and carried a three-shot advantage over Bryson DeChambeau into the final round.

And the world number 69 rammed home his dominance on Sunday by firing the round of the day - a 10-under 62 - to finish on 30-under overall. Herbert won by six strokes from England's Tyrrell Hatton, who shot a 63, while American DeChambeau finished three shots further back in third.

Golf.title: Shin holds on to win Women's Scottish Open
Golf.summary: Jenny Shin survives a tricky final round to see off fellow South Korean A-Lim Kim and win the Women's Scottish Open.
Golf.body:
Jenny Shin survived a tricky final round to see off fellow South Korean A-Lim Kim and win the Women's Scottish Open at Dundonald. Shin hit three bogeys on the front nine in a three-over-par 75 to finish on nine under.

Kim, who carded a fine 68, was two shots behind, with Thailand's Pajaree Anannarukarn a further two strokes back in third. It was Shin's first title in more than 10 years and only her second on the LPGA Tour in 368 attempts.

Golf.title: 'It's so nice to be back': Suspended ex-LIV pro shines (again) at Senior Open

Golf.body:
When Pat Perez elected to join LIV Golf back in 2022, he didn’t think he’d ever have a chance to play PGA Tour-sanctioned events again. But with only a few months left on his Tour suspension, the now-former LIV Golf pro is eyeing a future career on the PGA Tour Champions.

However, Perez isn’t waiting until his suspension is up to make some noise on the Senior Circuit. At this week’s ISPS HANDA Senior Open Championship, Perez is not only in the field — he’s in contention. And it’s not the first time Perez has been in the mix at a senior major this season.

Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Kellie Stenzel shares five suggestions for getting the most out of your practice — without taking lessons. The post 5 suggestions for optimal practice without getting lessons appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I have the opportunity to watch golfers of all skill levels on the practice range. As an instructor, my teaching eye naturally scans the swings as players try to launch that little ball into the air and keep it straight.

It’s always fun to watch someone celebrate a great shot. What’s a little harder to watch is seeing the same mistake repeated over and over without any adjustment, often relying on hand-eye coordination or luck rather than sound technique.

Golf.title: Rising star Jackson Koivun leads 3M Open but Scottie Scheffler lurks
Golf.summary: One of the top young players in golf, Jackson Koivun, leads the 3M Open in Minnesota. But can he hold off Scottie Scheffler on Sunday? The post Rising star Jackson Koivun leads 3M Open but Scottie Scheffler lurks appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When Scottie Scheffler tapped in for birdie on the 18th hole Saturday — the final stroke of a superb seven-under 64 — he made it a seven-way tie for first place and officially changed the narrative of the 3M Open.

Eighty minutes later, Jackson Koivun rewrote it. Koivun fired a 10-under 61 — which included a record eight-under 28 on the back nine — and at 20 under holds the 54-hole lead at TPC Twin Cities. Long-touted as the game’s top rising star, the 21-year-old pro now has his best chance to prove it. He enters Sunday with a three-shot lead over Emiliano Grillo and Ben Kohles. Koivun and Grillo make up the final pairing and tee off at 1:40 p.m. ET on Sunday. Scheffler is six back.

Golf.title: Ryo Ishikawa used to be Blades Brown. He sees something different in golf's current teen star
Golf.summary: Ryo Ishikawa once walked in Blades Brown's shoes. But golf's former phenom sees something different in its current teen star. The post Ryo Ishikawa used to be Blades Brown. He sees something different in golf’s current teen star appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Seventeen years ago, Ryo Ishikawa made his PGA Tour debut. He was a 17-year-old global golf phenom who had already won on the Japan Tour and appeared to be headed to the top of the golf world. He first won on the Japan Tour at age 15, finished T20 at the Masters at 19 and was a top-50 player in the world at age 20.

Every shot Ryo Ishikawa hit and every second of his lengthy post-round press conferences were broadcast. Nicknamed “The Bashful Prince,” Ishikawa was expected to become a golf superstar. But as is often the case, golf had other plans. Ishikawa was a PGA Tour staple from 2012 to 2017. He had two runner-up finishes, nine top 10s and made more cuts than he missed. But he never found the winner’s circle, and a back injury led to a dip in play that caused him to lose his PGA Tour card in 2017. Ishikawa returned to the Japan Tour and rebuilt his body and his game. He now has 20 career wins on the Japan Tour and is playing as a full-time Korn Ferry Tour member this year as he looks to return to the PGA Tour for the first time in a decade.

Golf.title: With LIV Golf facing 'headwinds,' former major champ plans for new future
Golf.summary: Graeme McDowell knows that LIV is facing "headwinds" as it tries to secure a future after 2026. With that in mind, he's making other plans. The post With LIV Golf facing ‘headwinds,’ former major champ plans for new future appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
LIV Golf is running out of time, and Graeme McDowell is among the pros planning for an alternative golf future. Ever since the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund announced it would cease backing the breakaway league after 2026, LIV Golf has been trying to create a new future. But this week at LIV Golf U.K., all the talk has suggested that it’s getting late for the rebel outfit.

Earlier this week, Martin Kaymer told Today’s Golfer that the LIV Golf team event in Michigan is “highly unlikely” to be played. Jon Rahm said he was “optimistic” LIV would have a future past 2026 but wouldn’t give any specific reason for his optimism apart from saying he’s optimistic by nature. LIV Golf was dealt another blow earlier in the week when the Asian Tour, which had been a partner of LIV since its launch, agreed to a deal with the PGA Tour and DP World Tour.
Golf.copy:
LIV Golf is running out of time, and Graeme McDowell is among the pros planning for an alternative golf future. Ever since the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund announced it would cease backing the breakaway league after 2026, LIV Golf has been trying to create a new future. But this week at LIV Golf U.K., all the talk has suggested that it’s getting late for the rebel outfit.

Earlier this week, Martin Kaymer told Today’s Golfer that the LIV Golf team event in Michigan is “highly unlikely” to be played. Jon Rahm said he was “optimistic” LIV would have a future past 2026 but wouldn’t give any specific reason for his optimism apart from saying he’s optimistic by nature. LIV Golf was dealt another blow earlier in the week when the Asian Tour, which had been a partner of LIV since its launch, agreed to a deal with the PGA Tour and DP World Tour.

Golf.title: Living on a prayer: Has LIV Golf drawn its final breath in the UK?
Golf.summary: Living on a prayer: Has LIV Golf drawn its final breath in the UK? The Observer
Golf.body:
So this is how it ends, Calvin Harris tunes wafting across undulating Staffordshire countryside while Rome burns. Barring intervention by someone with both a fetish for burning the GDP of a minor nation and the ability to do so, these are the last days of LIV Golf, its British leg likely the third from last.

For all they self-identify as revolutionaries, LIV UK feels strikingly similar to any other professional golf event. You can buy overpriced gyros and lukewarm lager and filthy, naughty fries – fries that are frankly begging for it. Their fan village resembles any other; children’s games sponsored by corporations expediting humanity’s demise. The obvious addition is the music, obnoxiously blasted across most tees and greens, with players choosing their own walk-on themes, meaning Tyrell Hatton emerges to “I just want relief from my stress” from NF’s My Stress. It’s unclear what any of this adds, manufactured and forced hype adding little to an atmosphere which still seems remarkably golfy. Nobody appears to be enjoying themselves more because some mumble rap is being played slightly too loud. The only place this isn’t true is the 14th, a par three flanked by two stands called The Birdie Shack, the most darts-ified area, blaring Sweet Caroline and John Denver. Between groups, an indefatigable hypeman oversees a mini-game between members of a stag party, incoherently drunk but sober enough to chip footballs into undersized goals from 12 feet or so. Chase and Status are performing after play on Saturday, because of course they are. Equally, the noise isn’t constant or unavoidable – at one point I set myself on a particularly comfortable hillock beside the fifth for a breather and, the enduring professional that I am, having returned from the World Cup on Monday, woke up 20 minutes later.

Golf.title: Herbert Leads LIV Golf UK by Four With Nine Holes to Play
Golf.summary: Herbert Leads LIV Golf UK by Four With Nine Holes to Play golfpost.com
Golf.body:
Lucas Herbert is on the verge of making history at LIV Golf UK Presented by JCB, holding a four-shot lead over Bryson DeChambeau as he heads into the back nine of Round 3 at JCB Golf & Country Club in Rocester, Staffordshire. Should the 30-year-old Australian close out Sunday's final round from the front, it would mark his second wire-to-wire victory of the 2026 LIV Golf season.

Herbert arrived at the Staffordshire venue in fine form, having spoken of carrying momentum from The Open the previous week, and he wasted no time stamping his authority on the field. His opening 61 — nine birdies and an eagle, bogey-free — shattered the course record at JCB Golf & Country Club, which had previously stood at 62. "If you were going to pick days you were going to shoot 59, I wouldn't have thought today would've been the day," he said. "The golf course is a little firm...a bit of breeze out there kind of moved around. I'm pretty incredibly happy with 61."

It’s been a disappointing season for someone of the talent of Bryson DeChambeau. The two-time US Open winner entered The Open Championship looking to avoid becoming the first multiple-time major winner under 40 to miss all four major cuts in a single season. He did so, finishing T14, but it only papered over what has been a poor year at the biggest events.

It’s been slightly better on LIV, where DeChambeau has won twice this season, but Jon Rahm is still threatening to run away with the individual title, winning for the third straight season. DeChambeau may be LIV’s biggest star, but Rahm is clearly LIV’s best player.

Golf.title: Chasing historic 59, Michael Kim knew exactly how to handle the moment
Golf.summary: Michael Kim shot 59 to etch his name into the record books at the 3M Open on Friday, recording the 16th sub-60 round in PGA Tour history. The post Chasing historic 59, Michael Kim knew exactly how to handle the moment appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
BLAINE, Minn. — Sometimes, it behoves players to not think about the big picture. One shot at a time. Lots of golf left. Don’t look at the leaderboard. That sort of thing. A couple of weeks ago at the Evian Championship, Haeran Ryu tallied up her scorecard on the 18th green and was shocked when she realized she shot 60, the lowest major round in women’s golf history.

But as for Michael Kim? He knew exactly where he stood on Friday. The 33-year-old, world No. 57 torched TPC Twin Cities, never made a bogey and birdied his last four to shoot a 12-under 59 — just the 16th sub-60 score in PGA Tour history. At 14 under, he leads the 3M Open with the afternoon wave still to finish.

The 33-year-old had 12 birdies without a bogey to finish his second round in the lead, three shots in front of compatriot Ben Kohles.

Golf.title: Bettinardi turns the tables on the zero torque trend with new Hexperimental release
Golf.summary: Bettinardi is flipping the script on the putter market and turning one of their 'zero torque' Antidote shapes into a traditional hosel. The post Bettinardi turns the tables on the zero torque trend with new Hexperimental release appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Today’s putter market has been flooded with “zero torque” offerings. Earlier this year Bettinardi added more options to the market with 2 Hexperimental shapes, but this time they’re flipping the script. The new Bettinardi Hexperimental #2 adapts the high M.O.I. ‘Simply Balanced’ Antidote SB2 shape and converts it into traditional heel-shafted setup without “zero torque” technology.

“We’ve had a wide range of players in our Tour Department, from pros to elite amateurs, fall in love with the Antidote SB2, but zero-torque isn’t for everyone,” said Sam Bettinardi, president of Bettinardi Golf. “That’s exactly the gap the Hexperimental #2 was designed to fill.”

Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau misses the point as he directly addresses Open Championship controversy at LIV UK hitc.com
Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau bounced back well from the controversy he caused at The Open Championship last week with a round of 64 on day one at LIV Golf UK. DeChambeau was right in the mix to win The Open after he made a birdie on his final hole of the day on Friday to put him one shot adrift of the leader, Lucas Herbert.

Bryson DeChambeau was penalized two strokes by Open officials after he was deemed to have improved the playing area around his ball in the rough during his second round.

Golf.title: ‘Two holes and I’m there for the Claret Jug’: DeChambeau says two-shot penalty cost him Open
Golf.summary: ‘Two holes and I’m there for the Claret Jug’: DeChambeau says two-shot penalty cost him Open The Guardian
Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau believes he would have been “right there for the Claret Jug” if he had not received a two-shot penalty in the Open Championship last week at Royal Birkdale. DeChambeau made a positive start to last week’s tournament after opening with a 67 and then a 66 on Friday, but his second-round score was later adjusted to 68 after he was handed a retrospective two-stroke penalty at the 5th hole after a video review. The 32-year-old was punished after match officials ruled he had improved the area of his backswing by standing on and flattening some long grass.

DeChambeau was in the mix at the top of the leaderboard but he dropped from second to fifth in the standings after his bogey was subsequently turned into a triple bogey. The American protested against the decision and even threatened to pull out of the tournament, but he played through the weekend and made 69 in the third round before a final-day 72.

Golf.title: Herbert shoots 61, leads DeChambeau by 3; Ripper with 4-shot team lead at LIV Golf UK Presented by JCB
Golf.summary: Herbert shoots 61, leads DeChambeau by 3; Ripper with 4-shot team lead at LIV Golf UK Presented by JCB LIV Golf
Golf.body:
ROCESTER, England – Fresh off his career-best finish in a major, Lucas Herbert continued that momentum into Thursday’s opening round at LIV Golf United Kingdom Presented by JCB. In the process, he produced another career-best – a bogey-free 11-under 61, his lowest-ever round relative to par.

“First time I’ve had 11, so that’s kind of cool,” Herbert said. “That’s a fun one.” Definitely fun for the Ripper GC star, as he grabbed a three-shot lead at JCB Golf & Country Club after producing a round with nine birdies and an eagle. His closest pursuer is Crushers GC Captain Bryson DeChambeau, who shot an 8-under 64 that included a stretch of four consecutive birdies and another stretch of three straight birdies to go with his eagle at the par-5 sixth.

BLAINE, Minn. — As a Minnesotan — me, the author of this article — I can assure you Scottie Scheffler has done all of the right things in the Land of 10,000 Lakes this week. He went downtown with his family and stopped at a local coffee shop on Monday (we’re big on stimulating the urban economy), signed every autograph after his practice round on Tuesday and complimented fans on Wednesday.

“A few people that recognized me were very nice,” Scheffler said on Wednesday, about his Monday adventure into Minneapolis. “They asked for photos. I was with my family so I said ‘No, not right now.’ They didn’t make a face, or they were kind of like, No, no, I totally understand, thanks for being here. I was kind of taken back by how nice people have been so far.”

Golf.title: 7 things you're getting wrong about your Handicap Index
Golf.summary: The Handicap Index, designed to level the game's playing field, is golf's most useful metric. It's also widely misunderstood. We explain. The post 7 things you’re getting wrong about your Handicap Index appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
What’s your handicap? And do you know what it actually measures? A lot of golfers don’t. The game’s most useful metric is also one of its most misunderstood. Misconceptions abound about everything from the calculations behind what’s officially known as a Handicap Index to what those numbers represent.

Here are seven of the most common myths, clarified. (Don’t have a handicap? You can sign up for one here.) Myth No. 1: My Handicap Index is my average score Nope. Your Handicap Index isn’t based on your average round. It’s calculated using the eight best of your most recent 20 Score Differentials. It’s designed to reflect your playing potential — not what you typically shoot on a Saturday morning.

Golf.title: Ryan Fox wasted no time hitting his Open-winning putt. Here's why
Golf.summary: On this week's episode of Subpar, newly-minted Open champion Ryan Fox explained why it only took 22 seconds for him to hit his winning putt. The post Ryan Fox wasted no time hitting his Open-winning putt. Here’s why appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Ryan Fox won his maiden major championship in impressive fashion on Sunday at Royal Birkdale, birdieing four of his final six holes, including the 18th, where he hit a masterful approach to 11 feet and then drained the putt to claim the Open title by a single shot over clubhouse leader Cameron Young.

One of the most notable details of Fox’s final hole was the way he wasted no time over his life-changing putt. In fact, it took only 22 seconds after Fox’s playing partner, Sam Burns, tapped in for his par for Fox to send his winning putt on its way to the hole.

Golf.title: Here’s the prize money payout for each golfer at the 2026 LIV Golf United Kingdom event
Golf.summary: Here’s the prize money payout for each golfer at the 2026 LIV Golf United Kingdom event Golf Digest
Golf.body:
It’s been a while since we’ve seen LIV Golf in action and there have been plenty of headlines in the meantime. The last event was in early June and how the league is back this week with its event in the United Kingdom at JCB Golf & Country Club in Staffordshire, England. The usual cast will, for now, play for the overall $30 million purse with the winner taking home $4 million and the winning team splitting $3 million.

LIV Golf’s top draw, Bryson DeChambeau, was the biggest newsmaker last week at the British Open at Royal Birkdale, despite not winning. His rules fiasco late Friday was a sight to behold. But he’s in England looking for his third victory this season after wins in Singapore and South Africa. He’s second in the season-long standings behind Jon Rahm, who has won this year in Hong Kong and Mexico City but has been more consistent. Rahm can wrap up the individual season title if he wins and DeChambeau finishes in a three-way tie for second place or worse.

Charley Hull, one day before this week’s ISPS Handa Women’s Scottish Open, described what is required to succeed in links golf. She said she felt she was starting to become more comfortable with the style.

“If you look at like the British Open,” Hull said, “there’s a lot of elements in it, and like British Opens always have like so many different kind of winners. “So I feel like there is a little bit of luck involved and a lot of patience involved because you can get bad bounces, and you can get — have funky shots and stuff. So you just have to accept them and just kind of just deal with it.”

Golf.title: ‘Golf needs rivalries’: Rory McIlroy's former agent believes animosity between Masters champion and Bryson DeChambeau is good for the game
Golf.summary: ‘Golf needs rivalries’: Rory McIlroy's former agent believes animosity between Masters champion and Bryson DeChambeau is good for the game Belfast Telegraph
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy’s recent comments about Bryson DeChambeau at The Open Championship are exactly what golf needs, claims the Holywood star’s former agent Andrew ‘Chubby’ Chandler. McIlroy, in his usual forthright manner, described DeChambeau’s manner as ‘performative’ after the two-time US Open winner was involved in a rules dispute on day two at Royal Birkdale last week.

DeChambeau was assessed a two-stroke penalty for inadvertently improving his lie on the fifth hole, but it was his actions following that which drew McIlroy’s ire, the big-hitting American threatening to withdraw from the tournament in protest while also trying to get US President Donald Trump involved, which delayed the release of the third round tee times.

Golf.title: LIV Golf: Graeme McDowell has held 'positive' talks over DP World Tour return
Golf.summary: LIV Golf: Graeme McDowell has held 'positive' talks over DP World Tour return BBC
Golf.body:
Graeme McDowell says he has held "really positive" talks about returning to the DP World Tour next season and believes he is "fortunate" to have a route back into mainstream competition.

McDowell told BBC Sport that he and the tour have agreed to meet again in November to finalise plans for 2027 amid ongoing uncertainty over LIV Golf's future. The 46-year-old, who joined LIV in 2022, won 11 tournaments on the DP World Tour between 2002 and 2020.

Golf.title: 'I was not informed': H.S. golfer DQ'd from U.S. Junior Am for new rule breach
Golf.summary: High school golfer James Nagle was disqualified from the 2026 U.S. Junior Amateur for multiple breaches of a recently adopted local rule. The post ‘I was not informed’: H.S. golfer DQ’d from U.S. Junior Am for new rule breach appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The 2026 U.S. Junior Amateur has moved on to match play, and so far much of the attention has been on a competitor who narrowly missed out on the final rounds: Charlie Woods. The 17-year-old son of three-time U.S. Junior Am champ Tiger Woods lost in a 14-man playoff on Wednesday for the final two spots in the match-play portion of the event. His effort was made harder by an intrusive camera click from a spectator.

But another competitor, James Nagle, saw his hopes of a U.S. Junior Amateur triumph end much earlier. Rather than a result of his play, Nagle’s exit came in the form of a DQ on Monday, a result of breaching a rare, recently adopted rule.

Golf.title: How Ryan Fox, Shane Lowry, and Nico Echavarria choose their wedge set-ups
Golf.summary: Ryan Fox has a unique steep delivery that required the perfect RTZ grind at Royal Birkdale. Picking wedges is more about you than the ground. The post How Ryan Fox, Shane Lowry, and Nico Echavarria choose their wedge set-ups appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When championship conditions turn baked-out and firm, the knee-jerk reaction among amateur players is to instantly strip bounce off every wedge in the bag. And YES, it did happen a bit last week at Royal Birkdale with players getting low bounce wedge grinds built up “just in case”.

The logic seems sound on paper: tighter lies demand a lower leading edge to prevent the sole from skidding into the middle of the golf ball. On Tour, however, the response from the trucks is far more personal. While firm fairways and tight turf do trigger an influx of low-bounce wedge options across the field, a player’s delivery geometry, swing path, and wrist release play a far larger role in grind selection than ground hardness alone.

LIV Golf's 2026 season continues this week with its stop in the United Kingdom, the final international tournament before the final three events are scheduled for August in the United States. LIV Golf’s $40 million season finale scheduled for next month is in serious jeopardy. Martin Kaymer, who leads the Cleeks GC team on the breakaway league, has told TG that it is now “highly unlikely” the Team Championships at The Cardinal course in Michigan will go ahead.

That lengthy break was enforced after LIV postponed a regular season event in New Orleans in late June amid reported concerns about soaring temperatures and course conditions, and now the league could be plunged into further chaos.

Golf.title: LIV's team event on brink of cancellation, per captain Martin Kaymer
Golf.summary: "The whole season was a bit of a …" LIV captain Martin Kaymer told Today's Golfer, opening up as the league faces funding challenges. The post LIV’s team event on brink of cancellation, per captain Martin Kaymer appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Martin Kaymer, captain of LIV Golf’s Cleeks team, told reporters on Wednesday that it is “highly unlikely” the circuit will stage its August team finale in Michigan. The news was first reported by Ben Parsons of Today’s Golfer, who spoke with a “disappointed” Kaymer ahead of this week’s LIV Golf UK event.

It comes as the embattled league seeks to secure funding for next season following the withdrawal of Saudi support earlier this season. Kaymer said that he expects the next three LIV events — this week in England and subsequent events in New Jersey and Indianapolis — will go ahead as scheduled, but barring a sudden change, the team finale in Michigan, scheduled for the Cardinal at Saint John’s in Plymouth, Mich., won’t happen. (He put the chances at five percent.) An earlier event scheduled for New Orleans was postponed indefinitely.

Golf.title: Martin Kaymer claims LIV Golf season finale in doubt
Golf.summary: Martin Kaymer claims LIV Golf season finale in doubt RTE.ie
Golf.body:
Martin Kaymer has cast doubt on LIV's Team Championship season finale going ahead in another blow to the beleaguered Saudi breakaway series. Chief executive Scot O’Neil is leading the search for over €300million of new money after the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia announced it was withdrawing backing at the end of the year after spending almost €4bn since its inception in 2021.

O’Neil spoke to the team captains on Tuesday at this week’s LIV event in Staffordshire and two-time major winner Kaymer said the news was not particularly encouraging. "I know that Indianapolis (the final individual event) is most likely happening. There was a conversation yesterday: Michigan, highly unlikely. According to yesterday, it didn’t look good," he told reporters at the event.

Golf.title: For only $20, you can play this quirky six-time Open Championship site
Golf.summary: Musselburgh Links, a six-time Open site outside Edinburgh, Scotland, sits inside the Musselburgh Racecourse, on its sprawling infield. The post For only $20, you can play this quirky six-time Open Championship site appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I played a new course the other day — that is, new to me — a nine-holer with a bargain-basement green fee and a wide-open tee sheet. It’s in Scotland, outside Edinburgh and inside the Musselburgh Racecourse, on its sprawling, rumpled infield. I had heard people talk about the Musselburgh Links often over the years but finally got to it a couple days after Ryan Fox, get-on-with-it Kiwi golfer, holed his winning putt at the Open Championship at Royal Birkdale. Fox could play this par-34 course, a former Open venue itself, in under an hour. He plays fast and so does this course. When the Scots invented golf they didn’t mean for it to be an all-day activity. (While we’re young, mon — or do your sheep shear themselves?) I imagine the new Open champ would like it. I know Sandy Lyle, winner of the ’85 Open, digs its whole vibe.

Upon arrival I saw no signs for the pro shop or whatever so I walked through an open pathway to the track itself, the red-brick grandstands now behind me, lush grass track ahead. The whole place was pretty much asleep on this warm weekday afternoon, and the whole scene brought to mind a long-ago visit to Doubleday Field in Cooperstown, N.Y., on a still summer day when there was no game.

Golf.title: Aaron Wise is battling more than just the golf course
Golf.summary: Former NCAA champ and PGA Tour Rookie of the Year Aaron Wise left golf to focus on his mental health. Now he's ready to talk about it. The post Aaron Wise is battling more than just the golf course appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
BLAINE, Minn. — Aaron Wise thinks hard before he answers questions. He wants to actually answer them, because he wants you to understand, because he’s spent years trying to make sense of it himself. His press conference at the 3M Open on Wednesday was lengthy and vulnerable and thoughtful. He had a lot to say. But probably because Aaron Wise has had a lot to deal with.

“It’s a constant daily battle out here,” Wise said. Years ago, Wise was one of the brightest young stars on the PGA Tour. He was the 2016 NCAA champion, and as a 21-year-old rookie shattered the scoring record at the 2018 Byron Nelson and won PGA Tour Rookie of the Year. Then, five years later, he withdrew just days before the 2023 Masters to focus on his mental health.

Golf.title: The practice habit that's hurting your golf game without knowing
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Monique Thoresz explains why leaving headphones in while practicing could be hurting your game. The post The practice habit that’s hurting your golf game without knowing appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
You’ve probably seen it at your local driving range: golfers with headphones in, either taking a phone call or listening to their favorite playlist. Maybe they’re trying to relax, block out distractions, or make practice more enjoyable. While there’s nothing in the Rules of Golf that prohibits listening to music, as a coach, I recommend leaving the headphones in your bag during practice sessions.

Golf is a game that demands concentration. One of the most important skills every player needs to develop is the ability to stay focused despite distractions. On the golf course, you can’t control the conditions. There may be noise from nearby groups, changing weather, unexpected delays, or simply long periods of waiting between shots. Learning to accept those moments instead of trying to eliminate them is an essential part of becoming a better player.

Golf.title: Ryan Fox’s speedy pace was a marvel. Should more golfers step on the gas?
Golf.summary: Watching Ryan Fox motor his way to an Open Championship victory makes you wonder if more golfers wouldn’t benefit from picking up the pace. The post Ryan Fox’s speedy pace was a marvel. Should more golfers step on the gas? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
If you didn’t see Ryan Fox coming, that might be because relative to many of his grind-it-out, stuck-in-the-mud peers, Fox blazes around the course like a greyhound chasing a hare. Ask Scottie Scheffler, who played alongside Fox and Zecheng Dou in the third round of the Phoenix Open earlier this year — or at least Scheffler thinks he played with Fox. “We walk off the 9th tee, and he goes, ‘Foxy, it doesn’t even feel like you’re in the group,’” the newly minted Champion Golfer of the Year said Sunday evening at Birkdale. “It just feels like we’re playing in a two-ball, you hit it so fast. It’s just in the air.”

Fox has always played with haste, dating back to his teen days in Auckland, New Zealand, when he’d join his father, Grant, a New Zealand rugby great, on corporate golf outings and intentionally waste little time to ensure he wasn’t holding up his playing partners. That Fox processed things quickly — not just on the golf course but also on the cricket pitch and tennis court — also didn’t hurt. See ball, hit ball.

Golf.title: Rahm enters LIV Golf UK on cusp of a three-peat
Golf.summary: Rahm enters LIV Golf UK on cusp of a three-peat LIV Golf
Golf.body:
ROCESTER, England – Whether it happens this week in the UK or next month in the U.S., Jon Rahm likely will win his third consecutive LIV Golf season-long Individual Championship. Nothing is guaranteed as of now, but it seems inevitable – as inevitable as a top-10 finish whenever Rahm tees it up at a LIV Golf tournament.

Rahm could clinch the three-peat if he wins LIV Golf United Kingdom presented by JCB, provided his closest pursuer, Bryson DeChambeau, doesn’t finish solo second or in a two-way tie for second. If DeChambeau finishes in a three-way tie for second or worse, then Rahm would have enough points going into the final two regular-season tournaments in New York and Indianapolis to clinch the title, no matter what anybody else does.

Badminton.title: Taipei Open: Fresh Starts in Doubles
Badminton.summary: Taipei Open: Fresh Starts in Doubles BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
YONEX Taipei Open 2026 will provide an early glimpse of several intriguing new partnerships as established names embark on fresh chapters across the doubles disciplines. In men’s doubles, former mixed doubles world No.7 Hiroki Midorikawa joins forces with 19-year-old Yuto Nakashizu, while Indonesia’s Muhammad Rian Ardianto begins a partnership with Daniel Edgar Marvino. Ardianto, a former world No.1 alongside Fajar Alfian, will be looking to build momentum after featuring in a few tournaments with Rahmat Hidayat. Singapore’s mixed doubles specialist Terry Hee also ventures into the discipline, teaming up with Wesley Koh in the qualifying rounds.

The women’s doubles draw sees Maya Taguchi return to the discipline just days after reaching the China Open mixed doubles quarterfinals with Yuta Watanabe. The Japanese youngster will partner Misaki Kurashima while also competing alongside Watanabe.

Badminton.summary: China Open: For Chou, Age Only Another Opponent BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
When Chou Tien Chen first stepped onto the international circuit in 2007, Sunday’s opponent Toma Junior Popov was just nine years old. Nineteen years later, the Chinese Taipei veteran showed that experience, resilience and discipline can still outlast youth.

At 36 years and 200 days, Chou became the oldest player to win a Super 1000 title, defeating Popov 21-15 7-21 21-13 to lift the VICTOR China Open 2026 crown. It capped one of the finest weeks of his long career, having also eliminated top-seeded defending champion Shi Yu Qi and All England winner Lin Chun-Yi en route to the title.

Badminton.title: China Open: Liu/Tan Complete Unprecedented Treble
Badminton.summary: China Open: Liu/Tan Complete Unprecedented Treble BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Liu Sheng Shu and Tan Ning marked a watershed season at their home event VICTOR China Open 2026 on Sunday. The world No.1s etched their names into the history books after becoming the first women’s pair to capture three Super 1000 titles in a season since the HSBC BWF World Tour was introduced in 2018, sealing the milestone with a 21-14 21-19 victory over Yuki Fukushima/Mayu Matsumoto.

The triumph carried extra significance as the Chinese pair avenged their only defeat in a Super 1000 final, against the same Japanese duo at last month’s Indonesia Open. It also saw Liu and Tan emulate Wang Xiaoli/Yu Yang as the last home partnership to successfully defend the women’s doubles title in 2012, while extending China’s dominance in the event to a fifth consecutive edition.

The drift may have dictated play all week at VICTOR China Open 2026 but on Saturday it carried Toma Junior Popov into uncharted territory. The Frenchman battled from a game down to defeat eighth seed Victor Lai 14-21 21-12 21-15, earning his first victory over the Canadian in three meetings.

In the process, Popov became the first French singles player to reach a Super 1000 final. Just 24 hours earlier, the 27-year-old had broken new ground by becoming the first singles player from his country in 22 years – after Pi Hongyan in 2004 – to make the China Open semifinals.

Badminton.title: Popov makes French history
Badminton.summary: Popov makes French history Badminton Europe
Badminton.body:
SecondsToma Junior Popov produced the finest result of his career at Super 1000 level on Saturday, recovering from a slow start to defeat Canada’s Victor Lai 14-21, 21-12, 21-15 and become the first Frenchman to reach a men’s singles final at this level.

It was a performance built less on spectacle than adjustment. Lai controlled the opening game with his speed and directness, but Popov gradually changed the shape of the contest, extending the rallies, finding greater depth and forcing the Canadian to work harder for his attacking opportunities. By the deciding game, the Frenchman looked the more settled of the two and closed out a historic victory after another demanding three-game match.

NEW DELHI: Every BWF World Championships throws up a few surprise packages, and the 2026 edition in New Delhi (August 17-23) could be no different. While the spotlight will be on the established stars, these five young shuttlers have the form and pedigree to challenge for a podium finish.

Ayush Shetty (India) – Men's SinglesThe 20-year-old has enjoyed a breakthrough campaign, winning the 2025 US Open Super 300 before finishing runner-up at the 2026 Badminton Asia Championships, where he stunned three top-10 players, including Olympic silver medallist Kunlavut Vitidsarn. Making his World Championships debut, Ayush remains an outsider but has already shown he can trouble the world's best. Backed by home support, the Karnataka youngster could emerge as India's dark horse.

Badminton.title: China Open: Yamaguchi’s Constant Excellence
Badminton.summary: China Open: Yamaguchi’s Constant Excellence BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:

The win marked Yamaguchi’s second straight win over Wang after she snapped a six-match losing run against the world No.2 at the Singapore Open in May. It also avenged last year’s semifinal defeat to Wang at the same venue.

The BWF World Championships, set to take place in New Delhi from August 17 to 23, often witness unexpected upsets that reshape the badminton landscape. While established stars usually capture attention, emerging young players have previously seized opportunities to elevate their careers within a single tournament week.

According to a press release from the BWF World Championships, five underdogs stand out as potential surprise contenders at the 2026 event in India. He secured his first BWF World Tour title by winning the 2025 US Open Super 300 and reached the final of the 2026 Badminton Asia Championships, defeating three top-10 players including Paris Olympics Silver Medallist Kunlavut Vitidsarn before earning the silver medal. Although the World Championships will be his first event featuring world-class opposition in every round, Shetty’s height and confident attacking play, coupled with home crowd support in New Delhi, may aid him in making a deep run.

Badminton.title: China Open: Chou Stops Shi Streak
Badminton.summary: China Open: Chou Stops Shi Streak BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Three years of frustration finally gave way to triumph as Chou Tien Chen ended a nine-match losing streak against defending champion Shi Yu Qi, battling to a 21-14 12-21 21-15 victory in the VICTOR China Open 2026 quarterfinals on Friday.

It was the Chinese Taipei veteran’s first win over top seed Shi since the team event at the postponed 2022 Asian Games in September 2023, and one built on an aggressive game plan designed to unsettle the home favourite.

Badminton.title: Ghana Badminton signs MoU with Special Olympics Ghana to promote inclusive sports
Badminton.summary: Ghana Badminton signs MoU with Special Olympics Ghana to promote inclusive sports Ghanaian Times
Badminton.body:
The Ghana Badminton Association (GBA) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Special Olympics Ghana as part of preparations for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics and Paralympic cycle.

The landmark agreement aims to strengthen collaboration between the two organisations by creating greater opportunities for athletes with intellectual disabilities to participate in badminton while expanding access to coaching, competitions, technical training, and athlete development programmes across Ghana.

Badminton.title: China Open: Tide Turned
Badminton.summary: China Open: Tide Turned BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Title favourites Wang Zhi Yi and Chen Yu Fei turned the tables on familiar foes to book their VICTOR China Open 2026 quarterfinal places on Thursday. Two-time defending champion Wang ended a three-match losing streak against Korean Sim Yu Jin with an assured 21-16 21-15 victory, keeping alive her bid to become only the second player in tournament history to win three consecutive women’s singles titles after Jiang Yanjiao (2008-2010).

Having struggled to find answers in their previous meetings, Wang was pleased with the way she stayed composed when the pressure mounted. “Every match is a new one. You’ve just got to stay in the moment, focus on what’s in front and think about tomorrow when it comes,” said the world No.2.

Badminton.title: China Open: Outsiders Steal Show
Badminton.summary: China Open: Outsiders Steal Show BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Wednesday at VICTOR China Open 2026 served a reminder that rankings sometimes count for little, as a trio of inspired performances sent fancied second and seventh seeds crashing out in Changzhou.

The biggest statement came from Denmark’s Rasmus Gemke, who produced his best victory in years to stun men’s singles second seed Kunlavut Vitidsarn 21-13 8-21 21-19. The world No.30 held his nerve after the deciding game reached 19-all, sealing his first win over the Thai world No.2 in three years and his first victory against a top-five player since defeating then world No.4 Li Shi Feng at the China Masters in November 2023.

Competitor News.title: Revolut Secures Front-of-Shirt Sponsorship with Como 1907 in Major Fintech-Football Expansion
Competitor News.summary: Revolut Secures Front-of-Shirt Sponsorship with Como 1907 in Major Fintech-Football Expansion FF News
Competitor News.body:
Revolut has expanded its partnership with Italian football club Como 1907, becoming the Official Front-of-Shirt Partner for the 2026/27 season. The deal integrates Revolut Business into club operations and offers fans exclusive fintech-driven experiences, including ticket discounts and co-branded merchandise across matchday journeys.

How Does Revolut Integrate with Como 1907 Operations? Revolut Business serves as the operational backbone for the club, managing critical foreign exchange transactions and supplier payments through a unified platform. By moving beyond a traditional sponsorship, the fintech technology is embedded directly into the club's financial infrastructure. This allows Como 1907 to leverage real-time financial tools to handle the complexities of competing in the UEFA Champions League and Serie A.

Competitor News.title: Revolut upgrades Como 1907 deal with front-of-shirt sponsorship
Competitor News.summary: Revolut upgrades Como 1907 deal with front-of-shirt sponsorship SportsMint Media
Competitor News.body:
The global fintech company, Revolut, has strengthened its presence in European sport by becoming the front-of-shirt partner of the Serie A club, Como 1907, expanding a partnership that began in 2025 into one of the club’s flagship commercial agreements ahead of the 2026-27 season.

The upgraded partnership will see the Revolut logo feature on the front of Como’s men’s first-team shirts across Serie A, domestic cup competitions and UEFA competitions. It builds on the company’s existing role as the club’s banking and FX partner, a relationship established in July 2025 that marked Revolut’s first sports partnership in Italy.

Competitor News.title: Como 1907 Elevates Revolut to Front-of-Shirt Partner Ahead of Historic Champions League Campaign
Competitor News.summary: Como 1907 Elevates Revolut to Front-of-Shirt Partner Ahead of Historic Champions League Campaign Ministry of Sport
Competitor News.body:
Italian Serie A club Como 1907 has announced global fintech company Revolut to become its new front-of-shirt partner for the upcoming 2026/27 season. Officially unveiled alongside the launch of the club’s striking new adidas home shirt, the agreement marks an evolution from an initial partnership established in 2025, during which Revolut served as the official banking and foreign exchange partner supporting the organisation’s core financial operations, supplier transactions, and player transfer payments.

The upgraded front-of-shirt positioning places Revolut at the very centre of Como’s global brand presentation during a milestone year that will see the club compete in the prestigious UEFA Champions League for the first time in its history.

Competitor News.summary: Revolut becomes Como 1907’s Official Front-of-Shirt Partner Como 1907
Competitor News.body:
Como, July 27th 2026 – Revolut, the global fintech company with more than 75 million customers worldwide, and Como 1907 have today announced the expansion of their partnership, with Revolut becoming the club’s Official Front-of-Shirt Partner from the 2026/27 season onward. The agreement unites two challenger brands that have evolved beyond their core industries to become lifestyle-driven powerhouses, combining innovation, culture, and community to redefine how modern audiences engage with finance and football. Since the partnership launched in 2025, with Revolut serving as Como 1907's Global Banking and FX Partner, the two companies have built a robust operational foundation. With Revolut Business fully integrated into its financial operations, Como 1907 manages everything from supplier payments to complex foreign exchange transactions through a single, seamless financial platform. Revolut’s logo will now feature on the men’s first-team shirts across Italian and European competitions. This next phase marks the natural evolution of their partnership’s success, taking Revolut to the heart of the club's supporter journey.

The new 2026/27 Como 1907 kit featuring Revolut is available to purchase now. Building on a strong foundation, the partnership will now focus on deeper product integration and innovative fan experiences that strengthen the connection between supporters and the club. Fans can look forward to exclusive ticket discounts, co-branded products, tailored merchandise offers, and matchday activations featuring the Como 1907 team and coach Cesc Fàbregas.

Competitor News.body:
Topgolf announced Thursday the renewal of its longtime partnership with First Tee, the national youth development organization that uses golf to build character, confidence, and resilience in young people.

The Dallas-based sports and entertainment company said the renewed collaboration will continue leveraging its nationwide venues and First Tee’s programs to introduce more kids and teens to the game while fostering life skills.

Competitor News.title: Ritter Sport UK accelerates its convenience expansion through nationwide Parfetts partnership
Competitor News.summary: Ritter Sport UK accelerates its convenience expansion through nationwide Parfetts partnership Wholesale Manager
Competitor News.body:
Ritter Sport UK is accelerating its expansion across the convenience channel through a new permanent wholesale partnership with Parfetts, bringing five of its bestselling block chocolate flavours to all nine depots nationwide from this month.

The move forms part of Ritter Sport’s wider strategy to significantly grow its presence within the UK’s 50,000-strong convenience sector, making the brand more accessible to shoppers wherever they choose to buy chocolate. By increasing physical availability across convenience and independent retail, Ritter Sport aims to recruit new shoppers, build brand awareness and drive long-term category growth.

Competitor News.title: Ritter Sport UK accelerates its convenience expansion through nationwide Parfetts partnership
Competitor News.summary: Ritter Sport UK accelerates its convenience expansion through nationwide Parfetts partnership Talking Retail
Competitor News.body:
Rum Raisin & Hazelnut, Marzipan, Milk Whole Hazelnut, Dark Whole Hazelnut and Pistachio will now be available to Parfetts’ network of 1,950 Go Local stores and more than 6,000 independent retailers, giving retailers access to one of the UK’s fastest-growing block chocolate brands while offering shoppers greater choice through premium-quality chocolate and distinctive flavour innovation.

The new permanent listing gives independent retailers the opportunity to differentiate their confectionery fixture with a brand that continues to outperform the wider market. At a time when consumers are eating less chocolate but demanding far more from every bite, Ritter Sport believes convenience retailers are well placed to capitalise on growing demand for products that deliver genuine quality, flavour and value.
